title: Differential Equations
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: What is Order and Degree of a differential equation?
cards.a:
Order: The highest order derivative appearing in the equation.
Degree: The power of the highest order derivative when the equation is expressed as a polynomial in derivatives (free from radicals and fractional powers).
cards.hint: Order is ALWAYS defined; degree may not be defined.

cards.q: CRITICAL TRAP: When is the Degree of a differential equation NOT DEFINED?
cards.a: When any derivative (like dy/dx or d²y/dx²) appears as the argument of a transcendental function (such as e^(dy/dx), sin(dy/dx), ln(dy/dx)) and cannot be eliminated.
cards.hint: Example: d²y/dx² + sin(dy/dx) = 0 has Order = 2, Degree = NOT DEFINED!

cards.q: General Solution vs Particular Solution of a differential equation?
cards.a:
General Solution: Contains arbitrary constants equal to the order of the differential equation.
Particular Solution: Obtained from general solution by assigning specific values to arbitrary constants using initial/boundary conditions (contains ZERO arbitrary constants).
cards.hint: An n-th order DE has exactly n arbitrary constants in its general solution.

cards.q: How to form a differential equation from a family of curves?
cards.a:
1. Count number of arbitrary constants (say n).
2. Differentiate the equation n times.
3. Eliminate all n arbitrary constants using the original equation and its derivatives.
cards.hint: The resulting differential equation must have order n and zero arbitrary constants.

cards.q: Variable Separable method: Form and solution?
cards.a:
f(x) dx + g(y) dy = 0 ⇒ Integrate directly:
∫ f(x) dx + ∫ g(y) dy = c.
cards.hint: Group all x terms with dx on one side and all y terms with dy on the other side.

cards.q: Substitution for equations reducible to Variable Separable: dy/dx = f(ax + by + c)?
cards.a:
Put u = ax + by + c ⇒ du/dx = a + b (dy/dx) ⇒ dy/dx = (1/b) (du/dx - a).
Separates into: du / [ a + b f(u) ] = dx.
cards.hint: Example: dy/dx = (4x + y + 1)² ⇒ put u = 4x + y + 1.

cards.q: What is a Homogeneous Differential Equation?
cards.a: An equation of the form dy/dx = f(x, y) / g(x, y), where f(x, y) and g(x, y) are homogeneous functions of the same degree in x and y.
cards.hint: Check: f(tx, ty) = tⁿ f(x, y) for all terms.

cards.q: Substitution used to solve Homogeneous Differential Equation dy/dx = F(y/x)?
cards.a:
Put y = v x ⇒ dy/dx = v + x (dv/dx).
Separates into: dv / [ F(v) - v ] = dx / x.
cards.hint: After integrating, always substitute v = y/x back!

cards.q: Standard form 1 of Linear Differential Equation (LDE) and its Integrating Factor (I.F.)?
cards.a:
Form: dy/dx + P(x) · y = Q(x).
Integrating Factor: I.F. = e^(∫ P dx).
cards.hint: P and Q must be functions of x only (or constants). Coefficient of dy/dx must be 1!

cards.q: General Solution of standard LDE dy/dx + P y = Q?
cards.hint: Mnemonic: 'y times IF equals integral of Q times IF dx plus c'.

cards.q: Standard form 2 of Linear Differential Equation (in x)?
cards.a:
Form: dx/dy + P₁(y) · x = Q₁(y).
Integrating Factor: I.F. = e^(∫ P₁ dy).
Solution: x · (I.F.) = ∫ [ Q₁ · (I.F.) ] dy + c.
cards.hint: Used when dy/dx equation is non-linear in y but linear in x (invert to dx/dy).

cards.q: Exponent log identity for simplifying Integrating Factor?
cards.a: e^(ln f(x)) = f(x)  and  e^(k ln f(x)) = e^(ln [f(x)]ᵏ) = [f(x)]ᵏ.
cards.hint: Trap: e^(-ln x) = e^(ln x⁻¹) = 1/x, NOT -x!

cards.q: LDE Trap: What must you do before identifying P and Q in x (dy/dx) + 2y = x²?
cards.a:
Divide by x first to make the coefficient of dy/dx equal to 1!
dy/dx + (2/x) y = x ⇒ P = 2/x, Q = x ⇒ I.F. = e^(∫ 2/x dx) = e^(2 ln x) = x².
cards.hint: Identifying P without dividing by x causes 100% wrong I.F.!

cards.q: Bernoulli's Differential Equation (Reducible to Linear)?
cards.a:
dy/dx + P y = Q yⁿ ⇒ Divide by yⁿ: y⁻ⁿ (dy/dx) + P y¹⁻ⁿ = Q.
Substitute v = y¹⁻ⁿ ⇒ (1 - n)⁻¹ dv/dx + P v = Q, which is standard linear in v.
cards.hint: Dividing by yⁿ and substituting v = y¹⁻ⁿ linearizes the equation.

cards.q: Exact differential shortcuts: d(xy), d(y/x), d(x/y), and d(x² + y²)?
cards.a:
1. x dy + y dx = d(xy)
2. (x dy - y dx) / x² = d(y/x)
3. (y dx - x dy) / y² = d(x/y)
4. x dx + y dy = (1/2) d(x² + y²).
cards.hint: Spotting these exact differentials solves MHT-CET DE problems in under 15 seconds.

cards.q: Application: Population Growth / Natural Decay law?
cards.a: dx/dt = k x ⇒ dx/x = k dt ⇒ x(t) = x₀ · e^(kt), where x₀ is initial quantity at t = 0.
cards.hint: k > 0 represents population growth; k < 0 represents radioactive decay.

cards.q: Application: Half-life period of a radioactive substance?
cards.a: T = (ln 2) / k  (where dx/dt = -k x).
cards.hint: At t = T, quantity remaining is exactly half the initial amount: x = x₀ / 2.

cards.q: Application: Newton's Law of Cooling differential equation and solution?
cards.a:
dθ/dt = -k (θ - θ₀) ⇒ θ(t) - θ₀ = (θ_initial - θ₀) · e^(-kt),
where θ is body temperature, θ₀ is surrounding/ambient temperature, and k > 0.
cards.hint: Rate of cooling is proportional to temperature difference (θ - θ₀).

cards.q: Number of arbitrary constants in General Solution vs Particular Solution of order 3?
cards.a:
General Solution has 3 arbitrary constants.
Particular Solution has 0 arbitrary constants.
cards.hint: MHT-CET standard theoretical question: A particular solution NEVER contains arbitrary constants!

cards.q: Differential equation of all circles passing through origin and having centres on x-axis?
cards.a:
Circle equation: (x - a)² + y² = a² ⇒ x² + y² - 2ax = 0.
Differentiating: 2x + 2y y' - 2a = 0 ⇒ a = x + y y'.
Substitute a: y² - x² - 2xy y' = 0.
cards.hint: Order is 1 because there is only ONE arbitrary constant 'a'.

cards.q: Differential equation of all parabolas with vertex at origin and axis along positive y-axis?
cards.a:
Parabola: x² = 4ay ⇒ 2x = 4a y' ⇒ 4a = 2x / y'.
Substitute: x² = (2x / y') y ⇒ x y' - 2y = 0.
cards.hint: Degree 1, Order 1 differential equation.

cards.q: How to find Orthogonal Trajectories of a family of curves?
cards.a:
1. Find the differential equation of the family: F(x, y, dy/dx) = 0.
2. Replace dy/dx by -dx/dy.
3. Solve the new differential equation.
cards.hint: Every curve of the new family cuts every curve of the original family at right angles (90°).

cards.q: General solution of dy/dx = e^(x - y) + x² e^(-y)?
cards.a: dy/dx = e^(-y) [ eˣ + x² ] ⇒ eʸ dy = (eˣ + x²) dx ⇒ eʸ = eˣ + x³/3 + c.
cards.hint: Factor out e^(-y) to separate variables immediately.

cards.q: Solution of (x + y)² dy/dx = a²?
cards.a:
Put x + y = u ⇒ 1 + dy/dx = du/dx ⇒ dy/dx = du/dx - 1.
u² (du/dx - 1) = a² ⇒ u² du / (a² + u²) = dx ⇒ integrates to u - a tan⁻¹(u/a) = x + c ⇒ y - a tan⁻¹((x + y)/a) = c.
cards.hint: Classic reducible to variable separable textbook problem.

cards.q: MHT-CET shortcut: Order and degree of [ 1 + (dy/dx)² ]^(3/2) = 5 (d²y/dx²)?
cards.a:
Square both sides to eliminate fractional power: [ 1 + (dy/dx)² ]³ = 25 (d²y/dx²)².
Order = 2, Degree = 2.
cards.hint: Highest derivative is d²y/dx² (order 2), and after clearing radicals its power is 2 (degree 2).
